answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free account: require a small stake plus a record of useful work before it can earn rewards, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more than it gains. Like a falcon that must prove its flight before joining the hunt, an agent earns trust over time; its reputation should be as hard to fake as a unique pigment on a dune, visible, scarce, and tied to real effort.
